plan_owner_impacts.impact: The chip/bloom, no-sidebar Settings contract is superseded: all four concepts have a persistent left navigation, a Settings Home, a Settings Workspace and manager surfaces reachable by deep link.

274 settings across 11 categories and 56 subcategories carry state.source, state.scope, isDefault, restart, exposure and (where relevant) an effect note. Inventory values that cannot express requested-vs-effective are invalid.
Models carry capability evidence with freshness, observed availability, alias, priority and visibility. Fast/effort modes are never inferred from a model name.
A provider family holds several accounts and API connections at once, each with its own billing, health and sign-in identity; account selection never re-authenticates.
Installations are detected, not bundled. A CLI-owned credential is never shown as a PM secret and never gets a PM sign-in control; PM offers to launch the tool's own login.
OpenCode appears as a server-connection family with its own installation record and community-hosted note.
Media generation routes are settings with an unavailable state and a reason, not a hidden capability.
The model receives a compact effective projection; the context manager shows admission receipts and the precedence chain.
Notes carry provenance, verification state, half-life and recall; deletion and redaction are separate operations with receipts.
Personas carry scope, route and a copyable capsule; import is preview-then-apply.
Goal state, spend guards and time guards are settings with explicit effect notes.
Crew templates carry members and sustainable concurrency; concurrency is one governed number, not a per-screen control.
PRD and planning conversations pin a high-quality route by design; the route is never downgraded to save usage.
Same route policy as the Planning Wizard; both appear as ordinary settings rows with a cost effect note.
Ordered rules with pattern, verdict, scope and a test action; approvals and sandboxing are separate subcategories.
Writable paths, protected version-control internals, presets and grant expiry; 11 sections in the manager.
Custom commands carry a dry run; shortcut binding reports conflicts.
220 distinct action ids were exercised across the four concepts; 73 map onto the packet's candidate families, the rest need adjudication before minting.
Servers carry transport, protocol requested vs negotiated, approval mode and exposure counts.
Skills are installed; plugins are loaded; tools are exposed. Three lifecycles, not one list.
As above; plugin inspect/reload/remove are distinct operations.
Tool inventory reports what is installed, enabled, available, selected for a turn and actually invoked.
Detected servers with coverage and health; restart is an explicit operation with a receipt.
Formatter chain with a test action and a per-language override.
Editor and file-manager settings carry compare, reload and save-journal operations.
Test runs expose the last run log as a diagnostic, not as a status colour.
Worktrees, merge tests, Actions runs, job logs and secrets are separate managers with their own health.
Runtime detection plus registry credentials; switching runtime is a primary action with a receipt.
Volumes, retention, compaction and migration; a storage surface is only useful if it does not measure media spend.
Artifacts carry size, age, reveal and export; deletion previews before it deletes.
Update attempts carry outcome, rollback state and the frozen generation still in use by an open thread.
7 installation records with paths, versions, owners and update attempts; adoption of an existing installation is an explicit operation.

settings_inventory_impacts.detail: label, explanation, kind, current value, default, source, scope and restart. A row without a source cannot answer 'why is it this way'.

settings_inventory_impacts.impact: Requested vs effective is a first-class pair
settings_inventory_impacts.detail: PMData.routeDifferences carries requested, effective, reason and scope; an inventory that stores one value cannot express a policy override.
standard / advanced / expert / managed / diagnostic / unavailable — search can find a risky unavailable item without rendering it as an equally inviting default control.
safety, cost and performance effects are separate kinds so a concept can weight them differently without inventing new prose.

settings_schema_impacts.detail: An unavailable row without unavailableReason is invalid; the concepts render the reason, never a bare disabled control.
kind:'manager' rows carry managerId and resolve through PMManagerKit; an unresolvable pointer is a validation failure, not a dead link.

settings_schema_impacts.impact: restart is a value, not a badge
settings_schema_impacts.detail: restart: none | restart | reconnect drives the row's own disclosure.

command_id_impacts.impact: Read-only diagnostics that must not mint commands

command_id_impacts.detail: No chip/bloom surface exists in this build; alias only if the shipped catalog still binds it.
Usage is a boundary card in Settings; ownership of refresh is unresolved between Settings and the Usage owner.

The one manager the four designs are meant to disagree about.

schema_event_storage_impacts.impact: Update attempts are stored, not derived
schema_event_storage_impacts.detail: An installation carries its update attempts with outcome and rollback state; a thread can still be using a frozen generation after a failed update.

schema_event_storage_impacts.impact: Notice dismissal is persisted per concept
schema_event_storage_impacts.detail: dismissedNotices is a persisted key; a dismissed notice must not return on reload.
localStorage keys are namespaced by concept id so four concepts can be reviewed in one browser profile without colliding.

migration_supersession_impacts.evidence: No occurrence of 'bloom' in any file in this folder.

migration_supersession_impacts.with: The shell's panel is a review surface, not a settings detail pane.
Access modes are ordinary settings values with typed safety effects
migration_supersession_impacts.evidence: No occurrence of 'yolo' in any file in this folder.

migration_supersession_impacts.with: Typed state.source plus a required reason for unavailable rows.

slint_port_impacts.impact: No layout measurement in the model
slint_port_impacts.detail: shared/pm-store.js holds semantic state only; the DOM is measured at explicit checkpoints in shared/pm-sections.js, which is where a Slint ScrollView.viewport-y callback would sit.
Every surface renders from arrays and records, so long lists can be virtualised or segmented in Slint without changing the model.
Focus follows document order; no concept moves focus during an animation.
Entrance animations use animation-fill-mode: both; if the entrance never plays the content is simply visible — a property Slint's animation model requires.

slint_port_impacts.impact: Reduced motion holds a static ring
slint_port_impacts.detail: data-reduced-motion=1 removes transitions without losing state.

test_fixtures.note: 38 manager records; 37 registered builders plus the bespoke provider surface
Deterministic triggers for every required state; the demo state is part of the deep link.

deferred_named_owners.insertion_contract: A manager module registered through PMManagerKit.register(id, builder) returning the same ManagerSpec shape; Settings hosts it at #/m/manager-project-sync and links it from Server & hosts. Settings never implements the sync state machine.
deferred_named_owners.why_deferred: PACKET/07 forbids concept agents from modelling Project Sync state machines.

deferred_named_owners.family: Browser Runtime / Browser Program / Expert Browser
deferred_named_owners.insertion_contract: Registers as manager-browser with sections for workspaces, programs and the human-only AuthBrowser session; Settings shows profile and permission rows only, never DOM or capture surfaces.
deferred_named_owners.why_deferred: PACKET/07 marks the AuthBrowser session human-only and inspection-free; a Settings concept cannot demonstrate it honestly.

deferred_named_owners.insertion_contract: One policy manager registered as manager-performance; Settings surfaces the single governor policy and its observed phases, and must not add a second concurrency control anywhere else.
deferred_named_owners.why_deferred: PACKET/SOURCE_AND_PRECEDENCE_MAP requires exactly one governor policy owner; four concepts inventing editors would create four.

deferred_named_owners.insertion_contract: Provider installation rows already carry updateAttempt evidence; the release owner registers manager-updates and Settings links installation rows to it rather than duplicating rollback policy.
deferred_named_owners.why_deferred: Update/repair/rollback policy is highest-precedence canon in PROVIDER_CLI_FINAL_ADJUDICATION.md.

unresolved_questions.question: Does cmd.usage.refresh belong to Settings or to the Usage owner?
unresolved_questions.why_it_matters: Settings shows balances on a boundary card; if Settings can refresh them it becomes a second Usage client.

unresolved_questions.question: Is an installation shared by two provider families one record or two?
unresolved_questions.why_it_matters: PACKET/reference handoff lists it as an open decision; the fixture models it as one record with two family references.

unresolved_questions.question: What is the retention period for update logs and failed staged installations?
unresolved_questions.why_it_matters: Storage retention rows cannot be authored without it; the fixture uses 30 days as a placeholder value the owner must confirm.

unresolved_questions.question: Which installation-owner adapters are MVP versus later?
unresolved_questions.why_it_matters: Determines whether Settings shows a repair path or only a re-install path for a given family.

unresolved_questions.question: Is automatic update opt-in, opt-out or provider-specific by default?
unresolved_questions.why_it_matters: The concepts render it as an explicit per-installation choice with no global default, which is safe but may not be the intended shipping behaviour.
